## 1. Executive summary — what the prototype has verified end-to-end

The `tiny` preset (dense, **254,272 parameters**) is the
smallest config on the same code path that scales to larger models. This cycle
took it through the full prototype validation path; each item below is backed
by committed artifacts and/or regression tests on `main`:

| # | Cycle item | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Architecture** | Verified — 254,272-param dense preset builds, trains, and matches its spec (64 hidden, 2 layers, dense FFN); full unit suite for attention/RoPE/MoE/block paths | [baseline artifact](baseline-tiny-cpu.json) (model section), `tests/test_attention.py`, `tests/test_block.py`, `tests/test_moe.py`, `tests/test_rotary.py`, PR #5/#9/#10/#12/#13 suites |
| 2 | **Tokenizer** | Verified — byte-level BPE round-trips English and tiny-vocab text (regression-tested after the pre-tokenization fix) | `tests/test_tokenizer.py`, `tests/test_tokenizer_regression.py`, PR #2/#7 |
| 3 | **Data pipeline** | Verified — memory-bounded streaming path with lazy tokenized exports | `tests/test_data.py`, `tests/test_streaming.py`, PR #4/#8 |
| 4 | **Training** | Verified — loss decreases on the fixed synthetic corpus: 6.9463 (untrained eval) → **1.8025** in 100 steps; deterministic under seed | [baseline artifact](baseline-tiny-cpu.json) (full trajectory in JSON), `tests/test_training.py` (loss drops >1.5 nats), PR #5 |
| 5 | **Inference** | Verified — prefill logits == KV-cache decode logits exactly; coherent greedy decode; 0.993 ms/token via KV cache | [baseline artifact](baseline-tiny-cpu.json) (inference section), `tests/test_inference.py`, PR #9 |
| 6 | **Quantization** | **int8 viable at ~99.97%–99.99% logit similarity** (worst-case single-position cosine across int8 variants in [0.999734, 0.999981]; cosine mean per variant ≥ 0.999948); greedy generations identical to fp32 in all variants; 3.77–3.98× smaller | [quant artifact](quant-tiny-cpu.json), `tests/test_quantization.py`, PR #12 |
| 7 | **DDM (KV-tier)** | **MEMORY-ONLY TRADE: mechanism is correct, but no acceptable benefit at the tiny CPU scale.** — 87.7% persistent-KV RAM cut, but paired median throughput ratio 0.8152 (CI lower 0.8041) fails the ≥0.90 gate; recorded as a valid negative | [DDM artifact](ddm-tiny-cpu.json), `tests/test_ddm_kv_cache.py`, PR #13 |
| 8 | **Performance baseline** | Established — train 27,946.5 tok/s, prefill 1.75 ms, decode 0.993 ms/tok on the recorded CPU | [baseline artifact](baseline-tiny-cpu.json), `tests/test_benchmark.py` (determinism), PR #10 |

**Bottom line:** the prototype's full loop — config → model → tokenizer → data
→ training → KV-cache inference — is exercised and regression-tested on `main`,
and the two experiments quantization and DDM each carry a measured, committed
verdict. Per the cycle's exit rule, this report is the gate artifact: the
prototype is validated at its own scale, with the limits of that validation
stated plainly in §5.

## 4. DDM KV-tier experiment — external context

The tiny DDM result does not stand alone: it corroborates independent,
published measurements of KV-cache tiering (collected in the team note
`kv-tiering-refs.md`, 2026-09-02):

1. **Disk tiering loses at small scale** — the kv-cache-tiering-bench
   measurements show disk spill costing 129–226 ms per block at prompt_len=1024
   with real I/O + fsync; the reuse-probability threshold exceeds 1.0, i.e.
   disk never beats discard/recompute in that regime. Talos's DDM design uses a
   local file tier with fdatasync — the same regime.
2. **A CPU-RAM pinned pool is the only tier that ever wins** in those
   measurements (reload ≈ 1–2% of prefill cost at 0.5B–1.5B scale); no other
   tier appears in the optimal policy at any reuse probability.
3. **INT8 hurts CPU tiers** (dequant on reload is 5–6× slower than fp16) —
   corroborating the design's choice not to combine the cold tier with
   quantization.
4. **Tiering is a bandwidth problem at scale** — for GB-scale KV payloads,
   PCIe transfer can reach 86× prefill compute and dominate execution time
   (arXiv:2601.19910). Tiny's ~256 KiB cache (262,152 B
   resident peak) is about five orders of magnitude below where tiering has
   been shown to matter.

**Reading:** the tiny result — memory gate passes (87.7% ≥ 75%),
all quality guards exact (logit diff 0.0, loss delta 0.0, greedy agreement 100%),
but throughput ratio 0.8152 (CI upper 0.8440) fails the ≥0.90 gate —
matches the published expectation for a file-tier experiment at small scale
rather than contradicting it. Per the pre-registered rules (design §5), this is
recorded as a **valid negative outcome** and this line of prototype DDM work
stops unless a separately approved change materially alters the memory ratio.

## 5. What this report does NOT yet tell us

This is the honest scope of the validation. A decision to scale would still
need evidence this cycle deliberately did not produce:

- **Single scale, single machine.** Every number here is one model size
  (254,272 params) on one 2-thread CPU. Nothing measures how the
  architecture, throughput, or memory footprint behaves as hidden size, layer
  count, expert count, or context length grow. There is no multi-scale sweep —
  no evidence yet that the code path's performance characteristics carry to
  larger configs.
- **No GPU / accelerator numbers.** All artifacts are `torch 2.13.0+cpu` CPU
  runs. Absolute latencies and throughputs are specific to this Xeon box and
  thread count; only the correctness metrics (exact logit equivalence, cosine
  similarity, greedy agreement) transfer across hardware.
- **One synthetic corpus, one seed.** Training measurements overfit a fixed
  deterministic synthetic corpus; the loss values (e.g. 1.8025) say
  "the optimizer and backward pass work", not "the model models language".
  No natural-corpus training curves, no tokenizer-throughput or data-pipeline
  performance measurements are committed.
- **Quantization scope is narrow.** Weight-only int8/bf16 with CPU
  dequant-matmul at one model size; no weight+activation quantization, no
  grouped schemes beyond per-channel/per-tensor, no kernel-accelerated
  (GPU/AArch64) paths, and no end-to-end serving measurements. The "~99.97–99.99%
  similarity" verdict is a tiny-model correctness statement, not a quality
  guarantee at other scales.
- **The DDM verdict is scale-specific by design.** "No acceptable benefit" was
  measured for a ~256 KiB KV payload with full-attention recall on CPU; it does
  not test — in either direction — tiering behavior at large-context,
  large-payload regimes. No positive benefit has been demonstrated at *any*
  scale in this repo.
- **Inference scope is minimal.** Greedy batch-1 decode through the KV cache
  only: no sampling, no batching/continuous batching, no speculative decoding,
  no paging, no server.
- **No training-stage or evaluation evidence.** SFT/DPO/reasoning-style stages
  and evaluation harnesses are outside this cycle; nothing here measures
  downstream task quality.

In short: the prototype is verified *at prototype scale on this machine*.
Claims beyond that scale are not supported by these artifacts and would need
their own measurements before any scaling decision.
